a.summary: The new F06 javadoc states the JDK 26/27 read-ahead condition as "the inflater holds leftover input"; the actual condition is leftover input greater than 26 bytes, and the difference is exactly the case the harness relies on available() for.
a.failure_scenario: A maintainer trims FragmentedInputStream.available() (or replaces the stream with one whose available() returns 0) on the strength of this sentence, reasoning that the inflater always holds some leftover after a member so read-ahead happens anyway. On JDK 26/27 the concatenated-member modes then silently return only the first member and fuzzHttpBody/the seed replay fails with "stream route returned the wrong body in mode 2" — the exact regression the sentence was written to prevent.

b.summary: The restated available() rationale states the JDK 26/27 read-ahead gate as "the inflater holds leftover input" when the actual gate is more than 26 bytes of leftover input.
b.failure_scenario: Exactly the body the patch's own new test builds is a counterexample: member + 10-byte bad-magic tail read through a 4096-byte buffer leaves `available() == 0` and `inf.getRemaining() == 18`, and JDK 26/27 do **not** read ahead, contradicting "or the inflater holds leftover input". Anyone reasoning from this sentence about why the concatenated-member mode is JDK-stable will conclude read-ahead happens whenever any bytes are buffered, which is false below 27 leftover bytes.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
